package_info.package_manager: N/A (system package, not a language package manager)
package_info.package_versions: All releases since 5.x up to patch (prior to 8.3.8, 8.2.20, 8.1.29)
package_info.why_malicious: The package is vulnerable due to a flaw in character encoding conversion ('Best-Fit' feature) in CGI mode, allowing unauthenticated remote attackers to inject command-line arguments via specially crafted HTTP requests. This enables arbitrary PHP configuration changes and remote code execution, making the default configuration of PHP CGI on Windows highly dangerous.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (upon receiving a crafted HTTP request by the web server)
execution_context.file_location: php-cgi.exe (invoked by web server, typically via ScriptAlias in Apache configuration)

malicious_snippets.code_language: shell (process invocation via HTTP argument injection)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the web server receives a specially crafted HTTP request, the PHP CGI process is invoked with injected command-line arguments, enabling dangerous PHP settings and causing the server to execute arbitrary PHP code supplied in the HTTP request body, resulting in remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior allows unauthenticated remote users to inject PHP configuration options and execute arbitrary code, which is a critical remote code execution vulnerability.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, web servers should not allow user input to influence command-line arguments for backend processes. PHP CGI should not accept arbitrary -d options from HTTP requests.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: PHP administrators may use -d options for local debugging or configuration during manual invocation, but never via untrusted user input from HTTP requests.
key_indicators: Unexpected -d options in PHP CGI process invocation
auto_prepend_file=php://input enables direct execution of code from HTTP request body
allow_url_include=on is a high-risk setting rarely enabled in production environments

execution_context.trigger: runtime (HTTP request with crafted query string exploiting Best-Fit encoding)
execution_context.file_location: php-cgi.exe (invoked by web server, typically via ScriptAlias in Apache configuration)

malicious_snippets.code_language: HTTP request (URL encoding exploiting Windows Best-Fit mapping)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the attacker sends an HTTP request with a query string containing special characters (such as %AD) that, due to Windows Best-Fit encoding, are interpreted as command-line argument prefixes by PHP CGI, allowing injection of dangerous PHP options and leading to remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of non-ASCII characters in the query string to bypass input validation and inject command-line arguments is a clear exploitation of the encoding flaw, enabling remote code execution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Web applications should not interpret URL-encoded characters as command-line arguments to backend processes. Query strings should not be able to alter PHP configuration at runtime.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate reason for user-supplied query strings to be mapped to process arguments in this way; such mappings should be strictly controlled.
key_indicators: Presence of %AD or similar non-ASCII bytes in query string
Query string values resembling PHP -d options
Unexpected PHP configuration changes at runtime via HTTP request

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts and sends an HTTP request with a query string containing special characters (e.g., %AD) and PHP -d options to the web server.
attack_chain.leads_to: PHP CGI process receives and interprets injected arguments due to encoding flaw

attack_chain.action: PHP CGI process, due to Windows Best-Fit encoding, misinterprets the query string and applies the injected -d options, enabling dangerous PHP settings.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary PHP code from the HTTP request body is executed on the server

attack_chain.action: Attacker's PHP code (supplied in the HTTP request body) is executed with the privileges of the web server process, resulting in full remote code execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: System compromise, data theft, or further malware deployment

behavioral_signatures: PHP CGI process invoked with unexpected -d options from HTTP requests
auto_prepend_file=php://input or allow_url_include=on set at runtime via command-line arguments
HTTP requests with non-ASCII or percent-encoded characters in query string mapping to process arguments
file_indicators: php-cgi.exe or php.exe invoked from web-accessible directories
ScriptAlias directive exposing PHP CGI in Apache configuration files (e.g., httpd-xampp.conf)
network_indicators: Inbound HTTP requests with query strings containing %AD or similar non-ASCII bytes
Unusual POST requests with PHP code in the body targeting PHP CGI endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor web server logs for HTTP requests with suspicious query strings containing non-ASCII or percent-encoded characters (e.g., %AD) and PHP -d options. Audit process creation logs for php-cgi.exe or php.exe being invoked with -d allow_url_include=on or -d auto_prepend_file=php://input. Check for ScriptAlias directives exposing PHP CGI in Apache configuration files. Alert on any runtime changes to PHP configuration via command-line arguments, especially those enabling dangerous options such as allow_url_include or auto_prepend_file.
